author: Barát / Thomassen
label: Problem 1.1
statement: What relaxation of the red induced-subgraph conditions ensures a crumby-style blue/red coloring of every 3-connected cubic graph? Blue maximum degree stays at most one.
disposition: Exclude as an insufficiently specified endpoint: allowing arbitrary red paths trivializes a literal relaxation. Original conjecture is already false in the source; do not count another relaxation.

author: Cambie
label: Problem 2.2
statement: For every finite graph G, is its list packing number at most twice its list chromatic number?
disposition: Hold: a universal list-assignment problem, not reducible to one ordinary coloring witness. Nearby 2.1 and 2.3–2.11 are not padded as extra families.

author: Horák–Rosa, presented by Hahn
label: Conjecture 3.1
statement: For every k>=1, n=4k+1 and k-element subset S of {1,...,2k}, XP(2n,S) is (2k+1)-edge-colorable except the Petersen graph. Layer 1 uses S, layer 2 its complement, with a perfect matching joining corresponding vertices.
disposition: Hold: source attributes the question to 2005. Concrete certificate possible, but original 2005 body and closest successors not acquired; cannot certify an unresolved target.

author: Hahn
label: Problem 4.1
statement: Does an absolute c>=0 guarantee rc(G)=2 for every noncomplete n-vertex graph with delta(G)>=n/2+c? In particular, does c=0 work?
disposition: Hold: inspected 2609.11437v1 Question 1.1, Theorems 1.9/1.11 and Lemma 2.1. Full finite statement survives those theorems; logarithmic surplus or o(n^2) exceptional pairs does not answer it. Famous broad endpoint, no new solving mechanism here.

author: Mattiolo / Ma–Mattiolo–Steffen–Wolf
label: Problem 5.2
statement: Does there exist a 5-edge-connected 5-graph in which every pair of perfect matchings intersects? A 5-graph is 5-regular with every odd vertex cut of size at least 5.
disposition: Hold: direct finite witness route but source connects nonexistence to Fan–Raspaud. Original 2023 proof body not inspected; no constructive family found. Do not split edge-colorability and matching clauses into credits.

author: Schiermeyer
label: Problem 6.1
statement: Describe all triangle-free graphs of maximum degree at most 3 and chromatic index 4.
disposition: Park: broad classification contains all snarks; source gives edge subdivision of a triangle-free 3-edge-colorable cubic graph as a known class. Reproducing this class would not answer the question.

author: Caro–Tuza
label: Problem 7.1
statement: Decide in deterministic polynomial time whether an arbitrary finite simple graph admits Type A (earlier degree zero or odd at every vertex) or Type B (also permits an even earlier degree when later degree is zero); construct an order when one exists.
disposition: Rank 1 provisional: investigate Type A source-set compression. Problems 7.1 and 7.2 treated as one recognition/search family, with the literal Type B clause retained as an additional residual obligation.

author: Stembridge, presented by Brenti
label: Problem 1.1
statement: For every Coxeter system (W,S), is sum over reflections t in T of x^length(t) rational?
disposition: Hold: ordinary group growth rationality in the preceding paragraph does not imply rationality of the reflection sublanguage. No finite-state mechanism or closest-successor body acquired.

author: Karp
label: Open problem. Find sufficient conditions on a1
statement: For positive real a1,...,ad,b and positive integers m1,...,md, find sufficient conditions for the numerator A(x) in the displayed Miller–Paris transformed hypergeometric generating function to have only real (negative) zeros.
disposition: Park: asks for sufficient conditions, while already naming the d-Narayana class. A new parameter instance or routine multiplier bridge would not resolve a uniquely specified full endpoint. Distinct from Toeplitz stability; that neighboring question was not selected.

author: Saff
label: Equilibrium open problem for multi-dimensional annulus
statement: For d-2<s<d, determine the Riesz s-energy minimizing probability measure supported on {x in R^d:r<=|x|<=R}.
disposition: Hold: nonroutine analytic endpoint. Source quotes Riesz ball solution and cites 2108.00534 Appendix D.2; ball formula does not settle positive inner radius. No full inversion/positivity mechanism derived.

author: Nikolov
label: Conjecture (G.N.)
statement: For every nonnegative continuous even convex majorant on [-1,1], do its snake polynomials have nonnegative first-kind Chebyshev coefficients in the source orientation?
disposition: Exclude: exact semantic duplicate. Inspected cached primary proof body SnakeChebyshevExpansionRefutation.lean and problem explanation: degree-six explicit majorant, alternation and negative constant coefficient -459/274. No new investigation invested after match.

author: Shapiro
label: Conjecture 1. For any polynomial P
statement: For every polynomial of degree at least three whose roots are in convex position but not a regular polygon, the closure of zeros of all derivatives of all positive powers is a closed domain; all critical points are on its boundary; that boundary has no inflections and lies in the critical-value envelope of z-alpha P/P-prime, alpha in [0,d].
disposition: Hold: all four clauses are one family, not four scouts. Fixed-power derivative zeros alone cannot certify the closure boundary. No asymptotic boundary proof acquired.

author: Bille–Buchstaber–Spodarev
label: Conjecture 3. For
statement: For every alpha,beta in (0,1) and every pair of feasible-size dual fullerenes, equality of trace exp(alpha A+beta D) is equivalent to graph isomorphism.
disposition: Hold: concrete spectral collision or parameter crossing could refute this universal assertion. Same n is required for a cospectral pair; equality of adjacency spectra alone is insufficient because D is nonconstant on dual fullerenes. No certified pair obtained.

author: Bille–Buchstaber–Spodarev
label: How can one construct a uniform distribution
statement: Construct a uniform random isomorphism class among all n-vertex fullerenes for each feasible even n>=20, n!=22.
disposition: Exclude literal existence endpoint: Section 3.1 already supplies enumeration followed by a uniform integer. Efficiency is the substantive motivation but no exact complexity endpoint is specified. Do not claim solving the question by repeating Section 3.1.

author: Gupur / Linton
label: When g(x) and f(x) are non-constants
statement: Establish well-posedness and time-asymptotic behavior of the two-unit parallel redundant model displayed in Section 4, for nonconstant repair/failure rates g(x),f(x), with the stated transport equations, renewal boundaries and Dirac initial data.
disposition: Park: original model attributed to Linton 1976; rate hypotheses are not made precise enough at the question for an all-rates theorem. Constant-rate solution is explicitly covered. Do not invent coercivity assumptions and call them a full resolution.
